title: Recipe 60 — Fleet & teams (when one harness becomes forty)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Everything so far assumed one harness. This is the recipe for the day your team has forty.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — nothing committed is touched by a take.

beats.label: Type a harness
beats.cue: “Fleet discovery is just 'find every crewhaus.yaml under this root' — so let's give it one to find.”

beats.label: List the fleet
beats.cue: “Discovery by convention, not registration. Nothing had to be added to a central list.”

verify.note: discovers the scratch harness under this driver directory

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “One harness, found by walking the tree. Forty works the same way.”

beats.label: Show fleet status
beats.cue: “The status view is the one an on-call engineer opens first — health per harness, in one screen.”

verify.note: per-harness status across the discovered root

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “Same command whether it's one harness or the whole team's.”

groups.title: Beat 2 · fan a verb across the fleet

beats.label: Run doctor across the root
beats.cue: [needs-key] “fleet run takes an ordinary verb and applies it everywhere — the diagnostics you already know, at fleet scale.”

verify.note: doctor, fanned across every discovered harness. NOT offline: `crewhaus doctor` checks provider credentials, so with no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY every harness reports `unclassified failure` and `fleet run` exits 1. Verified: exit 1 without a key, exit 0 with one.

beats.label: Read the results
beats.cue: [needs-key] “One row per harness. The failing one is the one you go look at.”

beats.label: Read the upgrade contract
beats.cue: “fleet run upgrade needs --allow-mutations, because a fleet-wide write is exactly the thing that should be hard to type by accident.”

verify.note: the shipped fleet-run flags, including the mutation opt-in

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “Read-only by default, mutating only on request. That's the right default for forty repos.”

beats.label: Read the propose contract
beats.cue: “propose diffs a candidate spec against the current one and writes the change up — a PR description you didn't have to draft.”

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “Spec changes are behaviour changes. They deserve the same review a code change gets.”

beats.label: Read the promotion contract
beats.cue: “deploy promote --require-approval --check-pr. Staging to prod, gated on a human and a green PR.”

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “The approval is the feature. Everything else is plumbing.”

beats.label: Rehearse a retirement
beats.cue: “--dry-run first, always. Retiring a harness someone still depends on is the fleet-scale version of deleting a table.”

verify.note: reports what retirement would do; changes nothing

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “Nothing was archived. That's what dry-run means, and it's why it's the default gesture.”

beats.label: Read the knowledge-sync contract
beats.cue: “What one harness learns, the fleet can pull. --push and --pull, deliberately separate verbs.”

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “Automatic push would mean one harness's bad lesson becomes everyone's. Pull is the safe direction.”

beats.label: List the plugins
beats.cue: [needs-key] “And the shared surface underneath it all — plugins the whole fleet can draw on. This one talks to a registry, so it needs one configured.”

verify.note: queries the configured plugin registry over the network; fails without a reachable registry base URL

beats.label: Search the marketplace
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Same registry, a query instead of a listing — recipe 26 is the whole story on that surface.”

verify.note: network call against the plugin registry

beats.label: Read the one-view summary
beats.cue: “fleet status, one view; fleet run, one verb everywhere; knowledge sync, one shared memory. That's the whole recipe.”
